properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dev-toolchain dependency: truffle 4.0.1 → elliptic 6.4.0 → hash.js 1.1.3 in the ArrayUtilsLib truffle lockfile. Provides the SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512 primitives elliptic uses internally (HMAC-DRBG, point hashing). No application call site — the product is Solidity libraries; the package exists only to run the local dev/test chain and coverage tooling. Changeable here by upgrading the dev dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev-toolchain dependency inventory: crypto-js 3.1.8 enters via web3@0.18.4 (requires crypto-js 3.1.8) inside the truffle 4.0.1 tree used to run the local test chain. The MD5 module ships inside the library; no application call site — deployed Solidity libraries never invoke MD5. Changeable here by removing/upgrading the dev dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev-toolchain dependency inventory: SHA-1 ships inside crypto-js 3.1.8 (same web3@0.18.4 chain as the MD5 entry). No application call site — the Solidity product never hashes with SHA-1; the toolchain is dev-only. Changeable here by upgrading the dev dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev toolchain only: evp_bytestokey@1.0.3 arrives via browserify-aes@1.1.1/browserify-cipher@1.0.0/browserify-rsa@4.0.1 (the browserify crypto shims webpack pulls into truffle 4.0.1), identical tree in all 8 lib lockfiles. No application call site — the deployed Solidity libraries never derive keys with it; it is shim plumbing. The retroactive MD5-KDF risk would only materialise if the toolchain ever fed it real key material.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: npm package bcrypt-pbkdf@1.0.1 (bcrypt-based PBKDF used for OpenSSH encrypted private-key headers), bundled in the truffle 4.0.1 dev toolchain (request→http-signature→sshpk chain; requires tweetnacl@0.14.5) in 8 per-library lockfiles. Dev toolchain only — the Solidity contracts never invoke it. Changeable here by upgrading truffle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test-only fuzz randomness: pointerUtils.js generates random ether values and submit/withdraw coin-flips to fuzz the IICO valuation-pointer algorithm during truffle test runs. Not key material, and no on-chain security decision depends on it — the contracts contain no randomness (verified: no blockhash/block.difficulty anywhere in .sol). Reachability is the local test suite only; kept as a weak-random record with that limitation.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: npm package create-ecdh@4.0.0, the crypto-browserify ECDH shim built on elliptic@6.4.0, required by crypto-browserify@3.12.0 in the truffle 4.0.1 dev toolchain (8 identical lockfiles). Quantum-unsafe EC key agreement ships in the dependency tree; no ECDH call site exists in the Solidity contracts or JS tests. Changeable here by upgrading the toolchain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 provides Ed25519 signatures (plus NaCl box/XSalsa20-Poly1305 and X25519), required by bcrypt-pbkdf@1.0.1 inside the bundled sshpk/request subtree of the truffle 4.0.1 dev toolchain. Dev toolchain only; not exercised by the application. Same logical package as the tweetnacl library object.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 ECDSA provider for the dev/test toolchain (truffle 4.0.1 / ethereumjs-testrpc 6.0.3 sign local-chain transactions through the ethereumjs/elliptic stack). Quantum-vulnerable (Shor breaks secp256k1); migration ML-DSA-65. Not used by the deployed Solidity libraries themselves — no ecrecover anywhere in the .sol sources (verified: zero matches across the workspace). Changeable here by swapping the dev toolchain's signing library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl 0.14.5 (NaCl: X25519, Ed25519, XSalsa20-Poly1305, SHA-512) is a dev-toolchain dependency in the truffle lockfiles. X25519 here is capability-of-the-shipped-library, not an application key agreement — the Solidity product performs no DH. Shor-vulnerable; migration ML-KEM-768. Changeable here only by replacing the toolchain dependency.
